note: The two sets are nearly identical in claims, values, and quotes, and both read the page correctly. The only substantive difference is that Set A keeps the condition that the recursive single-pole low-pass filter is used for both the torque and pitch controllers, while Set B drops that condition even though its own quote contains it. Both sets correctly bind the controller goals, feedback input, filter equations, and turbine configuration. Neither set is wrong, so Set A wins narrowly on condition fidelity.
remarks: Both sets omit the filter-state definition x[n] = y[n-1] (Eq. 7-3a) and the variable definitions (y filtered speed, u unfiltered speed, n step counter, Ts discrete time step, fc corner frequency). Both render the Greek coefficient alpha as 'a', a minor notation substitution that does not change meaning. The two sets are otherwise byte-for-byte similar, suggesting a shared extraction pipeline with one condition field dropped in B.
